group_assessment.weighting: PubMed counts 2026-10-02: senior author Morton SU[au] 121 records, 1 intersecting WWOX (this paper). A neonatal genetics and environmental-epidemiology collaboration (clinical case-control ascertainment plus GWAS, i.e. mixed descriptive-clinical and computational). Ascertainment of spina bifida is clinical-expert; the WWOX content is a nominal locus plus a literature paragraph.

field_density.note: This paper is the only WWOX record for neural tube defect or spina bifida in PubMed, so nothing replicates or contradicts it.

multihop.note: All 25 references enumerated; the XML reference list carries no PMIDs, so the three WWOX-direct ones were resolved by title on PubMed (Chen 2004 WOX1 in developing murine nervous system; Iacomino 2020; Salah 2010). Iacomino and Salah have identity records; Chen 2004 is mentioned only. They support the Discussion paragraph, not the association.

entries.proposition: The WWOX variants are intronic: "coding region" in the abstract means the gene body.
entries.snippet: Three variants on chromosome 16 were within the 8th intron of WWOX

entries.proposition: Multiple testing was handled only by a suggestive threshold; no genome-wide threshold was applied.
entries.snippet: We addressed multiple comparisons by only considering loci above the suggestive threshold

entries.proposition: The technical replication replicated two loci, CNTN5 and CTNNA2; the WWOX locus is not among them.
entries.snippet: Two previously identified nominal loci were replicated using the imputed dosages computed on the Michigan Imputation Server

entries.proposition: The authors describe the analysis as hypothesis-generating and list small cohort and confounding as limitations.
entries.snippet: the potential for unmeasured confounding factors to modify the observed associations

entries.proposition: The abstract’s named SNP rs7184417 has its own statistics in Table S2 (OR 6.22, p 3.42E-06, imputation R2 0.78), distinct from rs28688166.
The lead WWOX SNP is imputed with R2 0.78 and has cohort allele frequency 0.22.
Cases and controls differ markedly in age at study visit.
